title: BIO 102 ( UNN ) : CHAPTER NINE ( CONTROL AND COORDINATION IN PLANTS )
subject: BIO 102

questions.question: Plants possess the capacity to coordinate internal and external activities as a result of which substances?
questions.explanation: Plants coordinate activities as a result of hormones or chemical substances.

questions.question: The movement of higher plants is chiefly in the form of bending, twisting, and which other action?
questions.explanation: Higher plant movements are chiefly in the form of bending, twisting, and elongation.

questions.question: Plants show two types of movement which include the automatic movement and which other type?
questions.explanation: Plants show automatic movement and paratonic movement.

questions.question: Automatic movements occur due to factors inherent in which location?
questions.explanation: Automatic movements occur due to factors inherent inside the plant body.

questions.question: Streaming movement of protoplasm is an example of which type of movement?
questions.explanation: Locomotive movements include streaming movement of protoplasm.

questions.question: Growth movements involve changes in the form and shape of a plant organ due to what type of growth?
questions.explanation: Growth movement is due to unequal growth on two sides of the plant organs.

questions.question: Epinasty is a type of growth movement where the upper surface of the organ shows more growth compared to which part?
questions.explanation: In epinasty, the upper surface shows more growth compared to the lower surface.

questions.question: Hyponasty occurs when the lower surface of the leaf in bud condition is more active than which part?
questions.explanation: Hyponasty occurs when the lower surface is more active than the upper surface.

questions.question: Circumutation occurs when an apex makes which type of growth around the axis?
questions.explanation: Circumutation occurs when an apex makes a rotational growth around the axis.

questions.question: Paratonic movements are classified into tactic movement, nastic movement, and which other type?
questions.explanation: There are three types of paratonic movements including tactic, nastic, and tropic movements.

questions.question: Phototactic movement is a response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Phototactic movement is a movement made in response to light.

questions.question: Chemotactic movement is a response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Chemotactic movement is a movement made in response to chemicals.

questions.question: Nastic movement is made in response to which type of stimulus?
questions.explanation: Nastic movement is a movement made in response to non-directional source of stimulus.

questions.question: Photonasty is a type of nyctinasty that is due to which factor?
questions.explanation: Photonasty is due to photoperiod.

questions.question: Thermonasty is a type of nyctinasty that is due to which factor?
questions.explanation: Thermonasty is due to temperature.

questions.question: Haptonasty is a movement in response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Haptonasty is a movement in response to contact.

questions.question: Seismonastic movement is due to loss or gain of what substance?
questions.explanation: Seismonastic movement is due to loss or gains of water.

questions.question: When growth curvature occurs in line with the source of stimulus, it is known as which type of movement?
questions.explanation: If it occurs in line with the source of stimulus it is known as orthotropic movement.

questions.question: Geotropism is a response to which factor?
questions.explanation: Geotropism or gravitropism is a response to gravity.

questions.question: Hydrotropism is a response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Hydrotropism is a response to water.

questions.question: Traumatropism is a response to which condition?
questions.explanation: Traumatropism is a response to wound or injury.

questions.question: Rheotropism is a response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Rheotropism is a response to water current.

questions.question: Electrotropism is a response to which stimulus?
questions.explanation: Electrotropism is a response to electric field.

questions.question: Plant growth substances occur in very low concentrations of approximately which range?
questions.explanation: They occur in very low concentrations of 10-6 to 10-5 mol/L.

questions.question: Hormones are transported within the plant through cytoplasmic streaming, slow diffusion, phloem, and which other tissue?
questions.explanation: Hormones are transported through xylem that moves water and mineral solutes.

questions.question: Abscisic acid acts as which type of hormone?
questions.explanation: Abscisic acid is a stress hormone that acts as an inhibitory chemical.

questions.question: Auxins positively influence cell enlargement, bud formation, and which other process?
questions.explanation: Auxins positively influence cell enlargement, bud formation, and root initiation.

questions.question: Auxins act to inhibit the growth of buds lower down the stems promoting which phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Auxins promote apical dominance by inhibiting the growth of buds lower down.

questions.question: Synthetic auxin herbicides like 2,4-D are most toxic to which plant group?
questions.explanation: Auxins in large concentrations are most toxic to dicots and less so to monocots.

questions.question: Cytokinins influence cell division and which other formation process?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins influence cell division and shoot formation.

questions.question: Cytokinins counter the apical dominance induced by which group of hormones?
questions.explanation: Cytokinins counter the apical dominance induced by auxins.

questions.question: Ethylene is a gas that forms through the breakdown of which amino acid?
questions.explanation: Ethylene is a gas that forms through the breakdown of methionine.

questions.question: Ethylene affects which process in fruits?
questions.explanation: Ethylene affects fruit-ripening.

questions.question: Gibberellins are important in seed germination by affecting the production of which substance?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins affect enzyme production that mobilizes food production used for growth of new cells.

questions.question: Gibberellins are used to induce organogenesis such as which type of root formation?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins are used to induce organogenesis e.g. adventitious root formation.

questions.question: Brassinosteroids are a class of polyhydroxysteroids that stimulate cell elongation and which other process?
questions.explanation: Brassinosteroids stimulate cell elongation and division.

questions.question: Salicylic acid activates genes that produce chemicals to aid in defense against which entity?
questions.explanation: Salicylic acid aids in the defense against pathogenic invaders.

questions.question: Jasmonates are believed to have a role in seed germination and affect the storage of which substance in seeds?
questions.explanation: Jasmonates affect the storage of protein in seeds.

questions.question: Polyamines are essential for plant growth and affect which cellular processes?
questions.explanation: Polyamines affect the process of mitosis and meiosis.

questions.question: Nitric oxide serves as a signal in hormonal and defense responses including which plant process?
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide serves as a signal in defense responses such as stomatal closure.

questions.question: Strigolactones are implicated in the inhibition of which plant process?
questions.explanation: Strigolactones are implicated in the inhibition of shoot branching.

questions.question: Sodium salicylate has been found to suppress the proliferation of which type of human cancer cells?
questions.explanation: Sodium salicylate suppresses proliferation of lymphoblastic leukemia cells.

questions.question: Jasmonic acid and methyl jasmonate have been found to induce what in a number of cancer cell lines?
questions.explanation: Jasmonic acid and methyl jasmonate induce cell death in a number of cancer cell lines.

questions.question: Synthetic plant growth regulators are artificial plant hormones commonly used in which technique?
questions.explanation: Synthetic PGRs are used in plant propagation from cuttings, grafting, and tissue culture.

questions.question: Synthetic auxin herbicides include 2,4-D and which other compound?
questions.explanation: Synthetic auxin herbicides produced include 2,4-D and 2,4,5-T used for weed control.

questions.question: Chlrocholine chloride (CCC) is applied to inhibit which plant process?
questions.explanation: Chlrocholine chloride is applied to inhibit stem elongation.

questions.question: Quaternary ammonium salt AMO 1618 is applied to cause which type of growth in treated plants?
questions.explanation: AMO 1618 is applied to cause bushy shape and stocking growth.

questions.question: Morphactins inhibit seed germination or growth of seedling and increase which condition?
questions.explanation: Morphactins inhibit seed germination or growth of seedling, increase bud dormancy.

questions.question: Nutation involves growth in the apex taking place in which manner?
questions.explanation: Nutation involves growth in the apex taking place in a zigzag manner.

questions.question: The rapid movement of leaflets in Mimosa pudica is caused by differential loss of turgor in which structure?
questions.explanation: Differential loss of turgor on the two sides of the pulvinus causes leaflets to close rapidly.
